page: Amazon Web Services is4gen.medium is a storage-optimized instance built on the Nitro System architecture. It features a single dedicated vCPU based on the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture operating at 2.5 GHz. The configuration allocates 6.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:6 vCPU-to-memory ratio, and includes a dedicated 937 GB local NVMe solid-state drive. Networking operates with a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses or dedicated graphics accelerators are included.

Benchmark results reflect the constraints of a single-core Graviton deployment alongside its high local storage density. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU throughput reached an average category score of 1499.99, while aggregate multi-core and Geekbench metrics placed in lower tiers due to single-threaded limits, yielding a Geekbench single-core score of 940.0. Memory bandwidth reached 19.51 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and 9.76 GB/sec on large-block writes. Application-level measurements recorded Redis operations at 1.21 million operations per second and static web throughput at 1.13 GB/sec.

The architecture provides substantial local NVMe storage relative to its single-thread compute allocation, providing high storage capacity per core. However, the limited processing throughput and lack of multi-core capacity constrain compute-intensive tasks, parallel data transformations, or high-concurrency request serving. Amazon Web Services is4gen.medium is best suited for lightweight database replicas, key-value stores, distributed logging nodes, and temporary caching workloads requiring substantial local high-speed disk space without heavy compute requirements.
description: Amazon Web Services is4gen.medium is a storage-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with a single dedicated 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 core at 2.5 GHz. The configuration provides 6.0 GB of memory alongside an integrated 937 GB local NVMe SSD and a 2 Gbps baseline network interface. It excludes hardware accelerators and complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Synthetic benchmarks show steady single-core processing with a stress-ng score of 1499.99, though aggregate multi-core and Geekbench ratings reflect the hardware limitations of a single thread. Memory bandwidth delivers 19.51 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads, and Redis operations register at 1.21 million operations per second. The primary trade-off centers on high local NVMe capacity paired with entry-level compute resources. Consequently, the instance is appropriate for cost-conscious, I/O-intensive storage tasks such as lightweight transactional databases, distributed storage nodes, caching layers, and log processing pipelines that do not demand extensive CPU concurrency.
